findings.problem: File I/O (fs::read_to_string) is fused directly into the data-loading function with no shell boundary. The function name load_sensors suggests domain logic but performs unbounded filesystem access.
findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (missing file, permission denied, path length limits) panics via unwrap, crashing the caller. I/O latency is unpredictable and unbounded on the hot path.
findings.fix: Split into a shell function that handles fs::read_to_string and returns Result<String, IoError>, then a pure parse_sensors function that consumes a string/slice and returns typed domain errors.

findings.problem: println! (stdout I/O) is embedded inside the pure data-mapping closure. Logging belongs in the imperative shell, not in data-construction logic.
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot suppress debug output. Output ordering is nondeterministic relative to data processing. The function is no longer pure or testable without capturing stdout.
findings.fix: Remove println!. Return parsed Record from the closure. If diagnostics are needed, the shell layer handles logging after parsing completes.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - unwrap on fallible I/O with no error handling.
findings.failure_mode: Missing file, unreadable file, or oversized file causes a panic that aborts the entire program. No caller recovery is possible.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> and propagate I/O errors with ? or map_err to a typed IoError variant.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - unwrap on fallible numeric parse with no error handling.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed input (non-numeric value in field 1) panics. Examples: "abc", empty string, or a numeric string exceeding u32 range.
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e))? or map_err to a typed ParseError::Invalid variant.

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 - lossy cast from u32 to u16. Values 65536 and above silently truncate.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value like 70000 wraps to 4464 in the u16 field. The Record stores a silently corrupted value with no indication of data loss.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfBounds)? instead of as cast. Or parse directly as u16: .parse::<u16>().map_err(...).

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked indexing into split result. If a line has fewer than 1 comma-separated field, this panics.
findings.failure_mode: A line like "orphan" with no comma produces parts with length 1, then parts[1] panics. A line with only a comma produces parts[0] as empty but parts[1] panics.
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and .ok_or(ParseError::MalformedLine) to get (name, value_str) with safe destructuring.

findings.problem: parts[1] - same unchecked indexing violation on the value field.
findings.failure_mode: Same as above - any line missing the second field causes a panic.
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and destruct into (name_str, value_str) instead of collecting into Vec and indexing.

findings.problem: I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/trim/parse), logging (println!), and domain construction (Record) are all fused into a single function. No Functional Core / Imperative Shell separation.
findings.failure_mode: Pure logic is impossible to unit-test in isolation. Error paths are all panic rather than typed recovery. No ability to swap in test fixtures without filesystem manipulation.
findings.fix: Extract parse_sensor_line(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> as a pure function. Create load_sensors(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> as the shell that handles I/O and delegates to the pure parser.

findings.problem: No error type exists. All failures surface as panics. No distinction between I/O errors, malformed input, invalid values, or type overflow.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish a missing file from a bad CSV value. No structured error recovery or reporting is possible.
findings.fix: Define enum SensorError { Io(std::io::Error), MalformedLine(usize), InvalidValue(usize, ParseIntError), ValueOutOfBounds(usize, u32) } and return Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError>.

findings.problem: No input size cap before allocation. A file with millions of lines triggers unbounded Vec growth, potentially exhausting memory.
findings.failure_mode: Out-of-memory kill by OOM killer on large input files. No back-pressure or validation of input size.
findings.fix: Accept a max_items parameter. Use try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| SensorError::Allocation)? before the loop. Enforce the cap during iteration.

findings.problem: .collect() into Vec<String> then .map indexing - unnecessary intermediate allocation and indexing. split(',') produces a Split iterator; collecting to Vec<String> allocates all fields even though only two are used.
findings.failure_mode: Memory overhead proportional to field count per line. Each line allocates a Vec<String> with all trimmed fields, even when only name and value are needed.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get exactly two borrowed string references, avoiding per-line Vec allocation entirely.

findings.problem: Record fields are pub, allowing callers to construct invalid Records (e.g., empty name, out-of-range value) bypassing any smart constructor.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants are not enforced. Callers can create Records with empty names or arbitrary u16 values that were never validated.
findings.fix: Make fields private. Provide a smart constructor or builder that validates name is non-empty and value is in-range. Or use a derive newtype pattern.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists. No benches/ directory, no Criterion or similar dependency in Cargo.toml.
findings.failure_mode: Performance cannot be measured or verified. Any claim about load_sensors performance is untestable folklore.
findings.fix: Add Criterion benchmarks with realistic input sizes. Measure allocation count, wall time, and throughput. Report workload, baseline, and target hardware.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sensors throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis
no second-ring evidence for any performance claim
no command evidence (cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test) was executed
no benches/ directory or benchmark dependency in Cargo.toml
residual_risk: Multiple BLOCKER violations remain: hidden I/O in pure logic, unwrap panic surfaces on I/O and parse, lossy u32-to-u16 cast with silent data truncation, unchecked indexing into split results, no typed error taxonomy, no input-size bounds before allocation, no functional core/shell separation, and no benchmark or verification evidence. This code is not Holzman-compliant and would block any bead delivery pipeline.
